category_title: Preschoolers with autism exhibiting high rates of unengagement and social-communication deficits
student_description: This student frequently slips into passive unengagement and exhibits rigid, stereotyped manipulation of objects rather than purposeful play. They do not naturally seek out social interaction, often using pointing to regulate others (e.g., pushing hands away) rather than to share interest. They require heavy adult facilitation and environmental structuring to build joint attention, as strict academic demands or physical prompting cause them to withdraw further.

criteria.rationale: Because the student does not naturally seek out social interaction, they require ongoing, structured environmental arrangements to facilitate peer and adult engagement.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes specific strategies for structuring the environment or activities to necessitate and support social interaction and shared attention.

criteria.criterion_name: Prioritization of Joint Attention and Play Goals
criteria.rationale: Focusing strictly on academic task completion leads to increased unengagement; long-term success requires explicitly targeting symbolic play and joint attention.
criteria.check: The long-term plan explicitly prioritizes the development of symbolic play and joint attention skills over strict adherence to academic or task-completion goals.
